message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $43 and a pink monopoly with three houses each. p2 is dangerous with dark blues and reds at two houses. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 has $579 and no monopoly. I cannot mortgage, build, or unmortgage. The only legal actions are trading with p2 or p4, selling houses, or ending the turn. My strategy is to keep the pink monopoly at three houses each.

I should not trade Pennsylvania Avenue to p4. That would let them complete the green set by buying Pacific Ocean, which would be dangerous.

I am on my own turn after paying rent. I will not sell houses; the three-house pink monopoly is too critical.

I am calculating the board distances to see how p2 can reach my pink properties from Reading Railroad.

p2 can reach my pink properties from Reading Railroad on rolls of 6, 8, and 9. With three houses each, St. Charles Place would cost $450, States Avenue $450, and Virginia Avenue $500.

p2 has $31 cash. Liquidating all six red houses and both dark blue hotels would yield $1,081. That is more than enough to cover the $450–$500 rent on my pink properties.

p2 would be forced to sell houses evenly to pay the rent, which would devastate their dark blue holdings. I will not sell my houses.

p4 is now on St. James Place and could roll into my pink properties next turn.

p4 is already past the pink properties and will not hit them until the next lap. p2 is the immediate threat from Reading Railroad. I have no debt and cannot afford to build, so ending the turn is the correct choice.

I am evaluating specific trade offers. St. James Place would not give p4 a complete orange set, and the B&O Railroad would arm p2 with four railroads. I will not trade away any of these properties.
